nodes.label: ICRR Journal Design Handoff
nodes.rationale: High fidelity handoff: colors, typography, spacing, borders, animation timings and all copy are final. Where this README and the HTML disagree, the HTML wins. Not final: the six author profiles and article body text.

nodes.label: Pre-Launch Honesty in Copy
nodes.rationale: The journal has not published anything yet and the copy is deliberately honest about that ('Issue 1 publishing 30 September 2026', 'Appointment pending', 'Recruiting') rather than filled with fake articles. Two sections are explicitly marked as design previews and hidden by a single showPreviewNotes flag.

nodes.label: Do Not Port the Prototype Runtime
nodes.rationale: ICRR Journal.dc.html is authored in a lightweight in-house template runtime with a React-like component class; it is a design reference, not production code. The prototype keeps all ten views in one file and swaps them with a `page` state variable purely so the whole thing previews in a single browser tab. Do not replicate that pattern, use real routes.
nodes.norm_label: do not port the prototype runtime

nodes.label: No Border Radius Anywhere
nodes.rationale: Every corner is square. This is intentional: it is what makes the site read as a print journal rather than a SaaS product.

nodes.label: One Shadow in the Whole Design
nodes.rationale: The toast alone carries box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(36,31,30,.28). No other box-shadow may appear.
nodes.norm_label: one shadow in the whole design

nodes.label: Three Rule Treatments
nodes.rationale: The print-journal character comes almost entirely from three rule treatments: double rule 3px double #5D1D21 under the masthead, under every page heading and as the drawer's left border; hairline 1px solid #E2DACB for card borders, table rows and list dividers; gold hairline 1px solid #C0A265 only on highlighted callouts, always with #FBF7EE fill.

nodes.label: Top Strip
nodes.rationale: Full-bleed maroon, cream at .82, 11px uppercase. On a narrow screen the two halves wrap onto separate lines and both centre; pushed apart they read as an accidental break.

nodes.label: Masthead Lockup Sizing
nodes.rationale: Sized by height at clamp(72px,9.5vw,92px) with width auto, not by a fixed box: the file is 2500x600 and the prototype's 454x126 box did not match that ratio, so object-contain letterboxed the artwork and it drew smaller than the number implied.

nodes.label: Sticky Nav, Two Variants at 860px
nodes.rationale: Layout is justify-content: space-between with the link row as flex: 1, NOT absolute positioning; an earlier version used position:absolute for Submit and the links ran underneath it. Inactive links keep a 2px solid transparent border so nothing shifts. The switch is driven by window.matchMedia('(max-width: 860px)') with a change listener, not by CSS display, because the two variants have different DOM. Resizing above 860px force-closes the drawer.

nodes.label: Mobile Drawer
nodes.rationale: Right-hand sheet min(86vw, 340px) with border-left 3px double maroon over a rgba(36,31,30,.5) scrim. Clicks inside the sheet must stop propagation or the scrim handler closes it. Hamburger bars morph to a cross on open.

nodes.label: Footer Brand Block
nodes.rationale: Uses lockup-stacked-white.png, the stacked lockup drawn for dark grounds, because it carries mark and wordmark in one transparent file so nothing sits beside it. Do not put a cream or white rectangle behind a lockup to make it legible on maroon; the plate looks pasted on. The file is cropped to its artwork, so breathing room belongs to the layout, not the file.

nodes.label: Toast
nodes.rationale: Fixed bottom 30px, centered, z-index 80, ink fill, cream text, the one shadow, slides up via icrrUp 300ms, auto-dismisses after 3600ms.

nodes.label: Continuous Announcement Ticker
nodes.rationale: The line slides continuously (icrrTicker, linear, infinite); it does not swap every 6000ms as the prototype did, because a swap takes a line away half way through being read. The track holds the three strings twice over and travels translateX(-50%) so the loop has no seam. Duration is 0.11s per character with a 30s floor, keeping speed constant however much there is to say. Pauses on hover and focus-within; ends softened by mask-image rather than a coloured gradient; collapses to static text under prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Authors Filter and Search
nodes.rationale: Six chips plus a search input. Search matches case-insensitive substring against name, affiliation, discipline, role, bio, research interests and publication titles. Live count reads '6 contributors' or '3 of 6 contributors'. The six profiles are placeholders that exist so filter, search, empty state and the profile route are all demonstrable.

nodes.label: Placeholder Toast Actions
nodes.rationale: Every action with no backend yet shows a toast rather than doing nothing. In the real build, wire these up or hide the affordance, do not ship the toasts.

nodes.label: About Page Review-Policy Copy Constraint
nodes.rationale: An earlier draft said every author receives written feedback; that was removed because the journal cannot guarantee it. The double-blind wording went the same way: the journal reviews what it publishes but does not run double-blind or formal peer review, so claiming either promised a process that does not exist.

nodes.label: "Our Team" Rename from "Editorial Board"
nodes.rationale: The nav label, page title, mobile drawer entry, footer link, and one news CTA all say 'Our Team' / 'Our team' / 'Meet the team'. Editor-in-Chief is intentionally absent from the editorial roles list because Ayla covers it in the core team.

nodes.label: Brand Guidelines (ICRR).pdf
nodes.rationale: Named in design-reference/README.md as the source of truth for colors and type; the 14-token palette and the two-family typography system are documented as deriving from it. Binary PDF, 356 KB, not text-extractable in this environment, so its internal contents are asserted only through the handoff README.

nodes.label: Component (DCLogic subclass)
nodes.rationale: Single React-like class holding all ten views. state = { page, authorId, filter, q, ann, toast, narrow, menuOpen }.

nodes.label: componentDidMount
nodes.rationale: Starts the 6000ms announcement interval, registers the matchMedia('(max-width: 860px)') change listener, and arms the reveal.

nodes.label: componentDidUpdate
nodes.rationale: On page change: window.scrollTo(0,0) and re-arm the reveal.

nodes.label: componentWillUnmount
nodes.rationale: Clears the interval, disconnects the IntersectionObserver, removes the matchMedia listener.

nodes.label: _reveal
nodes.rationale: Builds the IntersectionObserver with rootMargin '0px 0px -12% 0px'. Line 906 is the critical guard: if getBoundingClientRect().top < window.innerHeight * 0.92 the element is returned over and never hidden.

nodes.label: nav(page)
nodes.rationale: Returns a click handler that sets page, closes the menu, and clears authorId unless navigating to the author view.

nodes.label: closeMenu
nodes.rationale: Calls stopPropagation so the scrim handler does not double-fire.

nodes.label: note(msg)
nodes.rationale: Toast factory: clears any pending timeout before setting a new message, then auto-clears after 3600ms.

nodes.label: renderVals
nodes.rationale: Computes every template binding in one pass: page flags, nav handlers and gold underlines, the author matcher and visible list, filter chips, countLabel, the three placeholder toast handlers, and the deadline/expected props.

nodes.label: matches (author search predicate)
nodes.rationale: Discipline chip first, then a case-insensitive substring test over a haystack of name, affiliation, discipline, role, bio, joined interests, and joined publication titles.

nodes.label: STEPS / TIMELINE / TOC_PREVIEW / FACTS / REQS / CHECKLIST
nodes.rationale: The prototype's process, timeline, ToC preview, journal-at-a-glance facts, manuscript requirements and pre-submission checklist copy. STEPS, TIMELINE and FACTS still say 'Double-blind review', 'at least two reviewers' and 'Review: Double-blind', which the later copy rule 3 forbids.
nodes.norm_label: steps / timeline / toc_preview / facts / reqs / checklist

nodes.label: TEAM / ROLES
nodes.rationale: Three core team members and seven editorial roles; Editor-in-Chief deliberately absent.

nodes.label: PAGES / PAGE_TITLES
nodes.rationale: The single-file view switcher's page keys and the mobile nav's centered page name. Home maps to an empty title.

nodes.label: ICRR Journal Website Design Spec
nodes.rationale: Approved for planning, dated 2026-07-26. Two halves in one project: the 10-view public site and the backend plus admin panel that let a non-developer run it.

nodes.label: Technology Decisions and Rejections
nodes.rationale: Next.js 15 App Router because 10 views map to file routes and the admin needs a server; Tailwind v4 CSS-first @theme so tokens live as CSS variables and arbitrary values carry the one-off clamp() sizes verbatim; Netlify and Supabase because both are already in use; TipTap JSON for article bodies because editors will paste from Word; Resend for email; supabase-js with generated types so there is no second ORM. Explicitly rejected: static export, a headless CMS, porting the prototype runtime, the single-file page-state pattern, and a public user system.

nodes.label: Postgres Data Model
nodes.rationale: site_config (single row), disciplines, team_members, editorial_roles, authors, issues, articles, article_authors, announcements, ticker_lines, submissions, newsletter_subscribers. Dates render as 'TBA' when null, matching the prototype.

nodes.label: Default-Deny Security Model
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled on every table with no permissive policy as the baseline. Anon gets select only, scoped per table; submissions and newsletter_subscribers get none. Two-layer gate: middleware alone is not treated as sufficient because a server action is reachable by direct POST. Path obscurity via ADMIN_PATH is a second layer, not the control. Uploads validated server-side and filenames regenerated, never taken from the client. Rate limiting on public submission and newsletter endpoints.

nodes.label: Public Routes and Their Data
nodes.rationale: Rule: public pages import content only from src/lib/content/. No page touches Supabase directly.

nodes.label: Announcement Rotator (6000ms cycle)
nodes.rationale: Spec §9 keeps the prototype's swap-every-6000ms rotator with the interval cleared on unmount. Later superseded by the continuous CSS ticker documented in the handoff README and the root README.

nodes.label: Admin Panel Sections
nodes.rationale: Editing UI follows the journal's own visual language rather than introducing a second design system. Forms are server actions with Zod validation on the server; the client mirrors the same schema for inline errors.

nodes.label: Submissions and Email Flow
nodes.rationale: If Resend is unconfigured or fails, the submission is still stored and the failure is logged. A stored submission is never lost to an email problem. Newsletter upserts so a repeat signup is not an error. Where an article PDF is absent the affordance is hidden rather than shown as a dead link.

nodes.label: Spec Copy Rules (two)
nodes.rationale: The spec carries only two rules: no em dashes, and never promise reviewer feedback. The third rule, never naming a review model or a reviewer count, is added later in the handoff README and the root README.

nodes.label: Eight Build Phases
nodes.rationale: Scaffold, Schema, Chrome, Public views, Behavior, Admin, Submissions, Verify and deploy. Each phase ends in a working, reviewable state; rebuild merges to main at phase 8.

nodes.label: Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: Peer-review workflow, author or reviewer accounts, DOI/ORCID/Crossref, full-text search, multi-language, analytics. The schema does not preclude any of these; none is built now.

nodes.label: Open Items Blocking Deploy
nodes.rationale: Supabase keys, admin account, Resend key and verified sender, chosen ADMIN_PATH, real photographs, real author profiles. All owned by the client. These do not block building; they block deploying.

nodes.label: Deviation from Spec §14 (own Zod schemas first)
nodes.rationale: The spec sequenced the Supabase schema at phase 2 so views would be built against real types. The plan instead defines domain types as Zod schemas the project owns, and the Supabase layer added in plan 2 maps database rows into those same types. Benefits: no Docker or Supabase credentials are needed to build the entire public site, generated database types never leak into view code, and the data source stays genuinely swappable.
nodes.norm_label: deviation from spec §14 (own zod schemas first)

nodes.label: globals.css Tokens, Reset, Keyframes, Component Classes
nodes.rationale: Declares the 14 --color-* variables under Tailwind @theme, a global border-radius: 0 reset, the six icrr* keyframes, and .eyebrow/.rule-double/.btn-*/.panel/.card/.callout-gold/.field. #D2B67E is the one hex outside the 14 tokens, permitted because it appears exactly once as the gold button hover.
nodes.norm_label: globals.css tokens, reset, keyframes, component classes

nodes.label: tests/unit/tokens.test.ts
nodes.rationale: Guards the single highest-risk thing at scaffold stage: a mistyped hex propagates into every view. Asserts whitespace-normalised keyframe bodies, not just names, so a later task cannot silently alter a motion curve. Also asserts exactly one box-shadow declaration and a global border-radius reset.

nodes.label: Zod Domain Schema (src/lib/content/schema.ts)
nodes.rationale: SiteConfig, Discipline, TeamMember, EditorialRole, Author, Issue, Article, ArticleAuthor, Announcement, TickerLine, ProcessStep, TimelineEntry, Requirement, Fact, TocPreviewEntry. Types the project owns, so Supabase rows are mapped into them rather than generated types leaking into views.

nodes.label: Seed Data (src/lib/content/seed/*)
nodes.rationale: Every string copied verbatim from the prototype at cited line numbers, never paraphrased. Notable transforms: the prototype's trailing \n in two role values is a data artefact and must be dropped; publications move out of the author record into articles.ts joined by getArticlesByAuthor; ROLES.holder becomes statusLabel and ROLES.color becomes status; NEWS.ctaKey becomes a real href.

nodes.label: Content Accessors (src/lib/content/index.ts)
nodes.rationale: Every accessor is async from day one so plan 2 can swap the body for a Supabase query with no call-site change, and validates through Zod on the way out so a malformed seed fails loudly here rather than silently rendering wrong. Unknown slugs return null rather than throwing.

nodes.label: Author Filter and Search (src/lib/authors/filter.ts)
nodes.rationale: Extracted as its own task because it is the only non-trivial logic on the public site and the prototype's exact matching behaviour must be preserved. Produces buildAuthorCards, filterAuthors, publicationLabel, countLabel and the AuthorCard type.

nodes.label: armReveal (src/lib/reveal.ts)
nodes.rationale: Returns a disconnect function; paired with a <Reveal> wrapper rendering <section data-reveal>. The guard at prototype line 906 is the critical behaviour: an element already within 92% of the viewport height on arrival is never hidden, so nothing above the fold flashes blank.

nodes.label: UI Primitives (Container, Eyebrow, PageHead, Button, Panel, Callout, ImageSlot)
nodes.rationale: Container carries the 1180px content width and the 1400px wide variant; ImageSlot renders next/image when src is set, otherwise the dashed placeholder.
nodes.norm_label: ui primitives (container, eyebrow, pagehead, button, panel, callout, imageslot)

nodes.label: Tasks 7 to 16: The Ten Views
nodes.rationale: Home, About, Current Issue, Archives, Authors directory, Author profile, Our Team, Submit, Announcements, Article reading page. Each view gets one route file plus per-section components under src/components/site/<view>/ and a Playwright spec.

nodes.label: Task 17: Design Audit
nodes.rationale: The automated guard that turns the copy rules and visual constraints into failing tests rather than review comments.

nodes.label: ICRR Mark (2x2 Quadrant Monogram)
nodes.rationale: Standalone square brand mark: a 1000x1000 four-quadrant checkerboard spelling I / C / R / R in a high-contrast Didone-style serif. Square aspect and no wordmark make it the favicon / avatar / app-icon asset, legible at small sizes where the full journal name would collapse.

nodes.label: ICRR Horizontal Lockup (Full Name, Transparent)
nodes.rationale: Wide 2500x600 lockup: quadrant mark on the left, thin vertical hairline divider, then INTERNATIONAL COLLEGIATE RESEARCH REVIEW set on two letterspaced all-caps lines. Landscape ratio targets the site masthead / header bar and letterhead, where vertical space is scarce and horizontal space is not.

nodes.label: ICRR Stacked Lockup (Transparent)
nodes.rationale: Portrait-ish lockup: large quadrant mark centered above a horizontal rule, with the two-line centered wordmark beneath. Vertical stacking suits covers, title pages, print PDFs and narrow/mobile viewports where the horizontal lockup would have to shrink below legibility.

nodes.label: Four-Quadrant Checkerboard Monogram
nodes.rationale: The acronym is laid out as a 2x2 grid rather than a single line so the mark reads as a square. Reading order is left-to-right, top-to-bottom (I C / R R). The grid also evokes a bound page or a quadrant of a journal cover, keeping the academic register without literal book imagery.

nodes.label: Diagonal Reversed-Contrast Tile Pairing
nodes.rationale: Tiles alternate on the diagonal: top-left and bottom-right are oxblood ground with bone letterforms, top-right and bottom-left are bone ground with oxblood letterforms. The alternation is what makes the grid legible without any drawn gridlines - the color swap itself is the divider - and it guarantees every letter keeps a high contrast ratio against its own tile.

nodes.label: Oxblood + Bone Two-Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Deep oxblood/maroon (approx #5E1F22) against a warm bone off-white (approx #F5F1EC). Strictly two brand colors, no gradients or tints, so the identity survives one-color print, embossing and small-size rendering. The warm off-white avoids the clinical feel of pure #FFFFFF and signals paper stock.

nodes.label: Transparent-Background Asset Convention
nodes.rationale: Both lockups ship with alpha transparency (the _transparent filename suffix) so they can sit on any page background; the bone tiles inside the mark stay opaque, meaning the mark itself always carries its own light ground and never inverts incorrectly on a dark surface.

nodes.label: Horizontal / Stacked / Mark-Only Variant System
nodes.rationale: Three assets cover three aspect-ratio budgets rather than one asset being scaled: wide horizontal for headers, stacked for covers and narrow viewports, bare mark for favicons and avatars. Choosing by available space instead of by scaling keeps the wordmark's letterspaced caps above their legibility floor in every context.

nodes.label: Letterspaced All-Caps Serif Wordmark
nodes.rationale: 'INTERNATIONAL COLLEGIATE RESEARCH REVIEW' set in a transitional/Didone serif, all caps, with wide tracking and broken across two lines of roughly equal measure. Wide tracking plus caps is the conventional scholarly-press signal; the two-line break keeps the wordmark from becoming an unusably long single ribbon.

nodes.label: Charcoal Wordmark Ink (Off-Brand-Color Text)
nodes.rationale: The wordmark is set in near-black charcoal (approx #333A3D), deliberately NOT the oxblood used in the mark. Keeping oxblood exclusive to the mark stops the two elements competing, lets the mark stay the single accent, and makes the wordmark behave like ordinary body typography next to it.

nodes.label: Vertical Hairline Divider
nodes.rationale: A thin full-height vertical rule sits between mark and wordmark, aligned to the mark's top and bottom edges. It fixes the clear-space relationship so the two elements read as one lockup rather than two adjacent logos.

nodes.label: Horizontal Hairline Divider
nodes.rationale: A thin horizontal rule, narrower than the mark, separates the mark from the centered wordmark below. Same separator role as the vertical rule in the horizontal lockup, rotated 90 degrees to match the stacked axis.

nodes.label: Centered Vertical Composition Axis
nodes.rationale: Mark, rule and both wordmark lines share one centered axis, and the rule's width is keyed to the wordmark measure rather than the mark. Centering is the title-page convention this variant is aimed at, and contrasts with the horizontal lockup's left-aligned, baseline-driven arrangement.

nodes.label: Divider Rule Separating Mark from Wordmark
nodes.norm_label: divider rule separating mark from wordmark
